deck.name: Movies
deck.description: Film history, directors, actors and famous moments.

questions.prompt: Who directed Jaws (1975)?
questions.explanation: Jaws is often called the first summer blockbuster.

questions.prompt: What was Walt Disney's first full-length animated feature film?
choices: The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.explanation: Released in 1937.

questions.prompt: Which film won Best Picture at the first Academy Awards ceremony in 1929?
questions.explanation: Wings is a silent World War I aviation film. The only other silent film to win Best Picture is The Artist (2011).

questions.prompt: The Godfather (1972) was directed by Martin Scorsese.
questions.explanation: Francis Ford Coppola directed The Godfather. Scorsese’s best-known 1970s films include Mean Streets and Taxi Driver.

questions.prompt: Who played Jack Dawson in Titanic (1997)?
questions.explanation: Kate Winslet played Rose opposite him. Titanic won 11 Oscars, including Best Picture.

questions.prompt: Which film features the line "Here's looking at you, kid"?
questions.explanation: Humphrey Bogart's Rick says it to Ingrid Bergman's Ilsa.

questions.prompt: Which film won 11 Academy Awards, tying the record held by Ben-Hur and Titanic?
choices: Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World
The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
questions.explanation: It won all 11 categories it was nominated in.

questions.prompt: Who composed the score for Star Wars (1977)?
questions.explanation: He also scored Jaws, E.T., Jurassic Park and the first three Harry Potter films.

questions.prompt: What was Pixar's first feature film?
questions.explanation: Released in 1995, it was the first entirely computer-animated feature film.

questions.prompt: Who directed Pulp Fiction (1994)?
questions.explanation: Pulp Fiction won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1994. Tarantino shared the Best Original Screenplay Oscar with Roger Avary.

questions.prompt: Roma (2018) was the first non-English-language film to win the Oscar for Best Picture.
questions.explanation: Roma won Best Director, Cinematography and Foreign Language Film but lost Best Picture to Green Book. Parasite (2019) was the first non-English-language Best Picture winner.

questions.prompt: Which studio made Spirited Away (2001)?
questions.explanation: Spirited Away won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in 2003.

questions.prompt: Who directed Spirited Away?
questions.explanation: Spirited Away won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in 2003.

questions.prompt: Who directed and starred in Citizen Kane (1941)?
questions.explanation: Citizen Kane was Orson Welles's first feature film. He was 25 when he made it.

questions.prompt: In The Matrix (1999), which pill does Neo take?
questions.explanation: The red pill reveals the truth; the blue pill would have returned him to the illusion.

questions.prompt: In what year was the first Star Wars film released?
questions.explanation: It was later retitled Star Wars: Episode IV, A New Hope.

questions.prompt: Who played the Joker in The Dark Knight (2008)?
questions.explanation: Jack Nicholson played the Joker in Batman (1989), and Joaquin Phoenix played him in Joker (2019).

questions.prompt: Heath Ledger won an Oscar for his role in The Dark Knight after his death.
questions.explanation: He won Best Supporting Actor at the 2009 ceremony.

questions.prompt: Who directed Inception (2010)?
questions.explanation: Nolan also directed the Dark Knight trilogy and Oppenheimer (2023).

questions.prompt: In Jurassic Park, where do scientists find the dinosaur DNA?
choices: In ancient plant seeds kept in tar
In frozen bones found in Arctic ice
In fossilised eggs found in a desert
questions.explanation: In reality, DNA breaks down far too quickly to survive millions of years in amber.

questions.prompt: Which film won Best Picture, Director, Actor, Actress and Screenplay at the 1992 Academy Awards?
choices: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
questions.explanation: It won all five major categories for the 1991 film year. The ceremony took place in 1992.

questions.prompt: Who played the title role in Forrest Gump (1994)?
questions.explanation: Hanks won Best Actor for the role, his second win in a row after Philadelphia.

questions.prompt: Tom Hanks won the Best Actor Oscar for Cast Away (2000).
questions.explanation: He was nominated for Cast Away but lost to Russell Crowe for Gladiator. Hanks won Best Actor two years in a row, for Philadelphia (1993) and Forrest Gump (1994).

questions.prompt: Which Alfred Hitchcock film (1960) contains a famous shower scene?
questions.explanation: The blood in the scene is chocolate syrup, which looked right in black and white.

questions.prompt: What colour are Dorothy's slippers in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz?
questions.explanation: In L. Frank Baum's book they are silver. The film changed them to show off Technicolor.

questions.prompt: Who directed Schindler's List (1993)?
questions.explanation: Schindler's List won seven Oscars, including Spielberg's first for Best Director.

questions.prompt: Which actor has won the most Oscars for acting?
questions.answer: Katharine Hepburn, with four Best Actress awards.
questions.explanation: She won for Morning Glory, Guess Who's Coming to Dinner, The Lion in Winter and On Golden Pond.

questions.prompt: Who directed 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968)?
questions.explanation: Stanley Kubrick directed the film and wrote the screenplay with Arthur C. Clarke.

questions.prompt: Which 1927 Warner Bros. film starring Al Jolson is famous as the first feature with synchronized spoken dialogue?
questions.explanation: The Jazz Singer was mostly silent, but its synchronized songs and spoken lines, recorded with the Vitaphone sound-on-disc system, launched the talkie era.

questions.prompt: Who directed the Japanese epic Seven Samurai (1954)?
questions.explanation: Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai shaped many later action films, including the Western remake The Magnificent Seven (1960).

questions.prompt: Which 1985 film features a DeLorean car converted into a time machine?
questions.explanation: In Back to the Future, Doc Brown builds the time machine into a DeLorean DMC-12. The other three films were also released in 1985.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the ship's computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey?
questions.explanation: HAL 9000 runs the Discovery One spacecraft. MU-TH-UR 6000 is from Alien, WOPR from WarGames, and Skynet from The Terminator.

questions.prompt: In Casablanca (1942), what is the name of Rick's nightclub?
questions.explanation: Rick Blaine runs Rick's Café Américain. The Blue Parrot is the rival club owned by Signor Ferrari.

questions.prompt: Who played Maria in The Sound of Music (1965)?
questions.explanation: Julie Andrews starred as Maria shortly after winning the Best Actress Oscar for Mary Poppins (1964).

questions.prompt: Which film won Best Picture at the 96th Academy Awards in 2024?
questions.explanation: Oppenheimer won seven Oscars, including Best Picture and Best Director for Christopher Nolan.

questions.prompt: Which film won Best Picture at the 95th Academy Awards in 2023?
choices: All Quiet on the Western Front
questions.explanation: Everything Everywhere All at Once won seven Oscars, the most of any film that year.

questions.prompt: Which director won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay for his first feature, Get Out (2017)?
questions.explanation: Jordan Peele became the first Black screenwriter to win Best Original Screenplay.

questions.prompt: Which Pixar film follows a trash-compacting robot left alone on an abandoned Earth?
questions.explanation: WALL-E (2008) won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. Big Hero 6 is from Walt Disney Animation, The Iron Giant from Warner Bros., and Robots from Blue Sky.

questions.prompt: In Finding Nemo (2003), what kind of fish is Dory?
questions.explanation: Dory is a blue tang. Nemo and Marlin are clownfish, and Gill is a Moorish idol.

questions.prompt: Who played Indiana Jones in Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981)?
questions.explanation: Tom Selleck was the first choice for the role but was committed to the TV series Magnum, P.I., so Harrison Ford was cast.

questions.prompt: Which Alfred Hitchcock film topped Sight and Sound's 2012 critics' poll, ending Citizen Kane's 50-year run at number one?
questions.explanation: Vertigo (1958) placed first in the British Film Institute's 2012 Sight and Sound poll of critics.

questions.prompt: Hattie McDaniel became the first Black actor to win an Academy Award, for Gone with the Wind (1939).
questions.explanation: McDaniel won Best Supporting Actress at the 1940 ceremony for playing Mammy.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Black woman to win the Academy Award for Best Actress?
questions.explanation: Halle Berry won Best Actress at the 2002 ceremony for Monster's Ball.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win the Academy Award for Best Director?
questions.explanation: Kathryn Bigelow won for The Hurt Locker at the 2010 ceremony. Chloé Zhao and Jane Campion won later, in 2021 and 2022.

questions.prompt: In which 1984 film does Arnold Schwarzenegger first say "I'll be back"?
questions.explanation: The line comes from The Terminator, directed by James Cameron. Schwarzenegger repeated versions of it in many later films.

questions.prompt: Who composed the score for Sergio Leone's The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)?
questions.explanation: Ennio Morricone scored Leone's Westerns. He won a competitive Oscar for The Hateful Eight (2015).

questions.prompt: Who composed the score for Psycho (1960), including the screeching strings of the shower scene?
questions.explanation: Bernard Herrmann worked with Alfred Hitchcock on several films, including Vertigo and North by Northwest.

questions.prompt: Who composed the music for The Godfather (1972), including its famous love theme?
questions.explanation: Nino Rota, an Italian composer, also scored many Federico Fellini films. He won an Oscar for The Godfather Part II.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the cowboy toy who leads Andy's toys in Toy Story?
questions.explanation: Woody is a pull-string cowboy doll. Buzz Lightyear is a space ranger, Jessie a cowgirl, and Bullseye a horse.

questions.prompt: Who directed The Lord of the Rings film trilogy (2001–2003)?
questions.explanation: Peter Jackson filmed all three films at once in his home country, New Zealand.

questions.prompt: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, at the 2002 ceremony?
questions.explanation: Shrek beat the other nominees, Monsters, Inc. and Jimmy Neutron: Boy Genius. Ice Age was nominated the following year, and Antz came out before the category existed.

questions.prompt: In which city did the Lumière brothers hold their 1895 public film screening, often cited as the birth of cinema?
questions.explanation: The Lumières, who were based in Lyon, showed their films to a paying audience at the Grand Café in Paris on 28 December 1895.

questions.prompt: Which 1902 French film shows a space capsule landing in the eye of the Man in the Moon?
questions.answer: A Trip to the Moon (Le Voyage dans la Lune), by Georges Méliès
questions.explanation: Georges Méliès, a former stage magician, pioneered special effects such as stop tricks and multiple exposures.

questions.prompt: Who played Vito Corleone in The Godfather (1972)?
questions.explanation: Marlon Brando won Best Actor for the role and declined the award. Al Pacino played Michael, and Robert De Niro played the young Vito in Part II.

questions.prompt: Marlon Brando and Robert De Niro both won Academy Awards for playing Vito Corleone.
questions.explanation: Brando won Best Actor for The Godfather (1972). De Niro won Best Supporting Actor for The Godfather Part II (1974), playing Vito as a young man.

questions.prompt: Which was the first sequel to win the Academy Award for Best Picture?
choices: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
questions.explanation: The Godfather Part II won in 1975. The Return of the King became the second sequel to win, in 2004.

questions.prompt: In Back to the Future, what speed must the DeLorean reach to travel through time?
questions.explanation: The car must hit 88 mph while the flux capacitor draws 1.21 gigawatts of power.

questions.prompt: Who directed Parasite (2019), the first non-English-language film to win Best Picture?
questions.explanation: Bong Joon Ho won Best Director, Best Picture, Best Original Screenplay and Best International Feature for Parasite.

questions.prompt: Which Hollywood studio's logo features a roaring lion?
questions.explanation: MGM's lion, often called Leo, has appeared in its logo since the 1920s. Paramount uses a mountain, Columbia a woman with a torch, and Universal a globe.

questions.prompt: Who was the first actor to play James Bond in an Eon Productions film?
questions.explanation: Sean Connery starred in Dr. No (1962). David Niven played Bond in the 1967 Casino Royale spoof, which Eon did not make.

questions.prompt: Which 1979 film introduced Ellen Ripley, played by Sigourney Weaver?
questions.explanation: Ridley Scott's Alien introduced Ripley. Weaver earned an Oscar nomination for the sequel, Aliens (1986).

questions.prompt: When Avatar (2009) became the highest-grossing film worldwide, whose record did it overtake?
choices: Titanic, also directed by James Cameron
Star Wars, directed by George Lucas
Jurassic Park, directed by Steven Spielberg
The Dark Knight, directed by Christopher Nolan
questions.explanation: Avatar passed Titanic in early 2010, so James Cameron held the record with two films in a row.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the hidden African nation in Black Panther (2018)?
questions.explanation: Wakanda is T'Challa's kingdom. Zamunda is from Coming to America, Genovia from The Princess Diaries, and Sokovia from Avengers: Age of Ultron.

questions.prompt: The Shining (1980), directed by Stanley Kubrick, was adapted from a novel by which author?
questions.explanation: Stephen King published The Shining in 1977. He publicly disliked Kubrick's changes to the story.

questions.prompt: Which film won Best Picture at the 97th Academy Awards in 2025?
questions.explanation: Anora won five Oscars, four of them for Sean Baker, including Best Director.

questions.prompt: Meryl Streep holds the record for the most Academy Award acting nominations.
questions.explanation: Meryl Streep has 21 acting nominations and three wins.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the hopping desk lamp in Pixar's logo?
questions.explanation: The lamp comes from Pixar's 1986 short film Luxo Jr., which John Lasseter directed.

questions.prompt: Which 1988 Studio Ghibli film features a giant, furry forest spirit who rides a Catbus?
questions.explanation: Totoro became Studio Ghibli's logo. Kiki's Delivery Service came out in 1989, Princess Mononoke in 1997, and Castle in the Sky in 1986.

questions.prompt: Which silent film star created the character known as the Tramp?
questions.explanation: Chaplin's Tramp, with bowler hat, cane and baggy trousers, appeared in films such as The Kid (1921) and Modern Times (1936).

questions.prompt: In Citizen Kane (1941), what is "Rosebud"?
questions.explanation: The last scene shows the name on the sled Kane was playing with when he was taken from his home as a boy.

questions.prompt: Which 2008 film about a Mumbai teenager on a quiz show won the Academy Award for Best Picture?
choices: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
questions.explanation: Slumdog Millionaire, directed by Danny Boyle, won eight Oscars. The other three films were also nominated for Best Picture that year.

questions.prompt: The Wizard of Oz (1939) is in Technicolor from start to finish.
questions.explanation: The Kansas scenes are sepia-toned. The film switches to Technicolor when Dorothy opens the farmhouse door in Oz.

questions.prompt: Which filmmaker directed Pan's Labyrinth (2006) and won Best Director for The Shape of Water (2017)?
questions.explanation: Guillermo del Toro won Best Director and Best Picture for The Shape of Water at the 2018 ceremony.

questions.prompt: Which film festival awards the Golden Lion as its top prize?
questions.explanation: Venice awards the Golden Lion. Cannes awards the Palme d'Or and Berlin the Golden Bear. Toronto's top prize is chosen by audiences.

questions.prompt: What is a MacGuffin in a film plot?
questions.answer: An object or goal that drives the characters' actions but matters little in itself.
questions.explanation: Alfred Hitchcock made the term popular. The briefcase in Pulp Fiction is often cited as an example.
